lines.t: Taif Road is a significant component of the Riyadh city road network. It spans a total length of 15.4 kilometers, starting from its intersection with Jeddah Road and extending to the western end of Taif Road. This project aims to identify and implement plans to enhance the road network, ensuring safe and efficient access to current and anticipated developments in the western part of Riyadh.

Development of Taif Road Project is a large-scale infrastructure development, designed to address the growing transportation needs of Riyadh. Led by Royal Commission for Riyadh City (RCRC). This road will enhance the capacity of Riyadh’s transport network, optimize traffic flow, and provide a sustainable long-term solution aligned with the city’s strategic development plans.

During the reporting period, the Procurement Team prepared and submitted four (4) prequalification packages to support the project’s procurement and construction requirements. The submissions included:
Tamkeen (Deal Commn): Civil discipline supplier prequalification for the supply of raw materials and aggregates.

ACES – Arab Company for Laboratories and Soil: Prequalification of an independent third-party laboratory.
Al Rashid Trading and Contracting Company: Prequalification of the crusher plant located in Daharat Laban, Riyadh.

These submissions support the evaluation and approval of qualified suppliers, laboratories, and service providers, helping ensure the timely availability of required materials and testing services. Follow-up activities will continue to facilitate the review and approval process and maintain alignment with the project schedule.
Weekly Construction Progress Summary:

During the reporting period, steady progress was achieved on structural works across Junctions 01, 03, 05, and 07. Activities included piling and foundation works, excavation for pier foundations and abutments, installation of formwork, reinforcement, scaffolding, and shoring systems, as well as concrete pouring for pier foundations, columns, pier heads, blinding, and deck elements.

Progress was also maintained on deck and bridge-related works, including web concrete pouring, deck slab formwork and reinforcement, Abutment A2 wall works, soffit formwork, and waterproofing membrane application at Junctions 03 and 05. These activities continued in line with the planned construction sequence to support the overall structural progress of the project.

Significant progress was also achieved on road, drainage, and utility works along the main carriageway and east and west service roads. Key activities included stormwater pipe and box culvert installation, manhole and GRP pipe works, ITS and street-lighting duct banks, street-lighting foundations, trench backfilling, leveling and compaction, and asphalt removal up to subgrade level in preparation for the aggregate base course.

Overall, the project maintained consistent construction progress across multiple work fronts, with ongoing efforts focused on structural works, drainage networks, utilities, and road infrastructure to support the planned construction sequence and maintain alignment with the approved project schedule.

lines.t: Taif Road is a significant component of the Riyadh city road network. It spans a total length of 15.4 kilometers, starting from its intersection with Jeddah Road and extending to the western end of Taif Road. This project aims to identify and implement plans to enhance the road network, ensuring safe and efficient access to current and anticipated developments in the western part of Riyadh.

Development of Taif Road Project is a large-scale infrastructure development, designed to address the growing transportation needs of Riyadh. Led by Royal Commission for Riyadh City (RCRC). This road will enhance the capacity of Riyadh’s transport network, optimize traffic flow, and provide a sustainable long-term solution aligned with the city’s strategic development plans.
Reporting Period: 24 Oct – 30 Oct 2026

During the reporting period, the Engineering Team maintained steady progress in the preparation, coordination, and submission of shop drawings and Requests for Information (RFIs), in accordance with the approved project schedule and technical requirements. Continuous follow-ups were carried out on previously submitted documents to expedite the review and approval process and ensure the uninterrupted progress of site activities.

Junction three, Unit 1 – Post-Tensioning Shop Drawing (A1 to P2).

Upcoming Submissions:

Retaining Wall and Separator Wall Drawings (CH 0+000 to CH 3+000).

The remaining 11 open RFIs are primarily related to structural works. Continuous coordination meetings and follow-ups are being conducted with the relevant stakeholders to facilitate their timely resolution and closure.
Summary:

Overall, the Engineering Team continues to demonstrate steady progress, with a strong focus on the timely preparation and submission of engineering deliverables, proactive coordination among stakeholders, and effective resolution of technical queries. Ongoing efforts are directed towards obtaining pending approvals, closing outstanding RFIs, and ensuring that all engineering activities remain aligned with the approved project schedule and construction requirements.
Pre-Qualifications and Procurement:
Reporting Period: 24 Oct – 30 Oct 2026

During the reporting period, the Procurement Team continued to make progress in preparing and submitting supplier prequalification packages to support the project's procurement and construction requirements. A total of seven (7) supplier prequalification packages were submitted, covering Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical disciplines, as detailed below:
Civil Discipline – 2 Prequalification Packages:
Saint-Gobain Weber (SODAMCO): Supply of chemicals and building materials.
Sail Al Reyadha Saudi Industrial Company (SEIFCO): Supply of interlock blocks and kerbstones.
Electrical Discipline – 3 Prequalification Packages:
ROLACO Arabian Sounds & Lights: Supply of outdoor lighting fixtures.
Safe Line Trading: Supply of conduits, fittings, and LV cables.
Lighting Technologies Company (LITEC GLINTY): Supply of outdoor LED lighting fixtures and lighting design services.
Mechanical Discipline – 2 Prequalification Packages:
RAWABI AL MAHFAR Trading Company: Supply of pipes, hangers and supports, and HDPE and UPVC perforated pipes.
KEPCO Middle East Company, Riyadh: Supply of galvanized steel pipe hangers and supports.

These activities support the timely evaluation and approval of qualified suppliers, ensuring the availability of approved materials and resources for upcoming project activities. The Procurement Team continues to coordinate with the relevant stakeholders to facilitate the prequalification process, support construction requirements, and maintain alignment with the overall project schedule.
Weekly Construction Progress Summary:

During the reporting period, construction activities progressed across the main carriageway, service roads, and various junctions. Roadworks included excavation along the main carriageway from CH 1+100 to CH 1+400, subgrade preparation, application of MC-1 prime coat, and asphalt paving along the temporary service roads between CH 4+308 and CH 4+129, and CH 4+403 and CH 4+308. Additional activities included the installation of streetlight pole foundations from CH 1+300 to CH 1+600, retaining wall formwork and reinforcement on the east side from CH 0+300 to CH 0+400, separator wall foundation works at CH 0+800, dry utility crossing formwork and concrete works from CH 1+400 to CH 1+700, excavation for catch basins on the west side from CH 2+200 to CH 2+800, stormwater pipeline excavation along the east and west service roads, and dry utility duct excavation from CH 8+000 to CH 8+400. Removal of median kerbstones and interlocking pavers also commenced along the main carriageway at Junction 03.

At Junction 07 (CH 4+050), reinforcement installation for the deck top slab between Piers P4 and P5 on the west side continued, along with excavation for the MSE wall near Abutment A2. At Junction 05 (CH 7+300), formwork and reinforcement installation for the pier foundation progressed, together with the erection of shoring for the deck slab on the west side. At Junctions 05 and 03, concrete pouring activities for pier foundations, columns, and pier heads continued, along with the application of waterproofing membranes to pier foundations. Backfilling and compaction around pier foundations at Junction 03 were also carried out.

Additionally, geotechnical borehole drilling for Underpass 02 at CH 14+400 was undertaken as part of the ongoing investigation works. Overall, construction activities continued across multiple work fronts, with progress focused on road infrastructure, utility networks, drainage systems, retaining structures, and major junction structures.

lines.t: Taif Road is a significant component of the Riyadh city road network. It spans a total length of 15.4 kilometers, starting from its intersection with Jeddah Road and extending to the western end of Taif Road. This project aims to identify and implement plans to enhance the road network, ensuring safe and efficient access to current and anticipated developments in the western part of Riyadh.

Development of Taif Road Project is a large-scale infrastructure development, designed to address the growing transportation needs of Riyadh. Led by Royal Commission for Riyadh City (RCRC). This road will enhance the capacity of Riyadh’s transport network, optimize traffic flow, and provide a sustainable long-term solution aligned with the city’s strategic development plans.
Reporting Period: 31 Oct – 06 Nov 2026

During the reporting period, the Engineering Team maintained steady progress in the preparation, coordination, review, and submission of shop drawings, technical documents, and Requests for Information (RFIs), in accordance with the approved project schedule and technical requirements.

Continuous follow-ups were carried out on previously submitted documents to expedite the review and approval process, resolve outstanding technical comments, and ensure the uninterrupted progress of site activities. Coordination with the relevant project stakeholders and technical teams remained ongoing to address engineering requirements and minimize potential delays.
Key Engineering Submissions:
The following engineering documents and drawings were submitted during the reporting period:
Junction 7 – Deck Slab Setting-Out Drawing.
U-Turn Plan and Profile (+10.000 to +11.000).
Retaining Wall Reinforcement Shop Drawings.
Junction 5 – Deck Slab Setting-Out Drawing.
Junction 3 – Deck Slab Reinforcement, Unit 1 (A1 to P2).
Temporary Full Road Closure Plan for Junction 7 (STA 3+560 to STA 4+530).
ITS Manhole Formwork and Reinforcement Details.
Junction 3 – Deck Slab Reinforcement, Unit 2 (P2 to P5).
MSE Wall Panel Reinforcement Detail Drawings.
Pedestrian Bridge No. 4 – General Arrangement and Foundation Setting-Out at CH 5+366.
Traffic Management Plan for Underpass Construction Works (KM 11+000 to KM 15+000).
Typical Details for Separator Wall.
Pedestrian Bridge No. 4 – Pier and Elevator Foundation Reinforcement Shop Drawings.
Upcoming Engineering Submissions:
The Engineering Team is currently working on the preparation, coordination, and submission of the following upcoming deliverables:
Dry Utilities Layouts and Utility Network Drawings (CH 7+000 to CH 9+000).
Hardscape, Stormwater, and Cross-Section Drawings (CH 8+000 to CH 15+400).
Retaining Wall and Separator Wall Drawings (CH 0+000 to CH 3+000).
Pedestrian Bridge No. 5 – Engineering Drawings.
Structural Submissions for Junctions 1 and 3, including foundation, reinforcement, and setting-out drawings.
Additional Utility and Irrigation Layouts, Manhole Schedules, and Combined Utility Plans.
Softscape Drawings (CH 0+000 to CH 10+000).
Landscape and Hardscape Drawings (CH 8+000 to CH 15+000).
Request for Information (RFI) Status:
The RFI status as of the reporting period is summarized below:

The remaining eight open RFIs are primarily associated with structural works. Continuous coordination and follow-up meetings are being conducted with the stakeholders concerned and technical teams to address outstanding comments, facilitate timely responses, and achieve closure at the earliest opportunity.
Overall Summary:

Overall, the Engineering Team continues to demonstrate consistent progress in delivering the project's engineering requirements. Key efforts remain focused on the timely preparation and submission of technical documents, expediting pending approvals, resolving outstanding RFIs, and maintaining effective coordination with all relevant stakeholders.

The team remains committed to supporting ongoing construction activities, minimizing potential engineering-related delays, and ensuring that all engineering deliverables remain aligned with the approved project schedule, specifications, and technical requirements.
Pre-Qualifications and Procurement:
Reporting Period: 31 Oct – 06 Nov 2026
During the reporting period, the Procurement Team continued to make progress in preparing and submitting prequalification packages to support the project's procurement and construction requirements.
The submissions covered the Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, and Traffic disciplines, including:
Civil: Saad Gulf Consultant Engineers for design verification of concrete Jersey barriers, and NASRA GEOSYN (NGS) for the supply of geotextile materials.
Electrical: Riyadh Cables for the supply of electrical cables.

Mechanical: RAWABI AL MAHFAR Trading Company for the supply of pipes, hangers, supports, HDPE, and UPVC perforated pipes; and Hilti Saudi Arabia Construction Tools Co. for galvanized pipe hangers and support accessories for drainage pipes at abutments and pedestrian bridges.
Traffic: Shawahid Industrial Roads Company, KSA, for the supply of traffic safety products, including crash cushions.

These activities support the timely evaluation and approval of qualified suppliers and subcontractors, ensuring the availability of required materials and services for upcoming construction activities while maintaining alignment with the project schedule.
Weekly Construction Progress Summary:

During the reporting period, the Construction Team made steady progress across the major project work fronts, covering structural works at Junctions 01, 03, 05, and 07, as well as infrastructure and road works along the main carriageway and service roads.

Key activities included reinforcement installation, post-tensioning duct installation, formwork, and concrete pouring for deck slabs, pier foundations, pier heads, columns, and abutments. At Junction 07, progress continued on deck slab construction, pier works, Abutment A1 waterproofing, and MSE wall foundation excavation. At Junction 05, deck slab reinforcement and post-tensioning duct installation progressed, while structural works continued at Junctions 01 and 03.

Infrastructure activities included dry utility duct excavation, stormwater drainage works involving GRP pipe installation and manhole construction, and road separator wall construction. Retaining wall foundation works, including reinforcement, formwork, and waterproofing, also progressed. Additionally, subgrade material application continued along the main carriageway.

Overall, construction activities progressed across multiple work fronts, with continued focus on structural development, underground utilities, drainage systems, and road infrastructure in accordance with the project schedule.
